restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224 operations per sha256-r32 compression); the only random coins are N_b = 2^50.787 fresh uniform 64-byte first blocks; the tail table V (explicit conditions, chaining-value independent) is fixed and scanned in full for each of at most M = 2^36.685 accepted blocks; at most S_max = 2^46.5 survivors are continued; the budget is fixed before the run and fully charged.

Structural two-block ordinary collision: m = B0 || M1 and m' = B0 || M1' (128 bytes each), padded by the target rule into a common third block; standard IV, rounds 0..31 on every block including the padding block, feed-forward, all 256 digest bits compared.

Reuses unchanged the 36-step SHA-256 local collision and characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 (Tables 9 and 10; message differences in W5,W6,W7,W8,W9,W13,W14,W21,W23), whose support lies at step index <= 30, so 32-step evaluation enforces exactly its conditions; verified with the trusted reference on two published instances.

Charged time <= 2^53.0 target compressions as a worst case over the fixed budget: 2^50.79 first-block compressions charged 1.0674 each (all trials, accepted or not), 2^57.9 tail candidates charged 32 word operations each (incremental step-16 evaluation from precomputed chaining-value-independent state), 2^46.5 survivor continuations charged 4096 operations each, 2^40 preprocessing; worst-case total 2^52.43. Success probability >= 0.503 for this budget by Chernoff tail bounds and exp(-0.70) under the declared heuristics. Conservative fallback charging every tail candidate as a whole compression: 2^57.9.

Cryptanalytic claim below the nominal 128 reference; no full-scale execution is performed and no colliding certificate is provided. Parameter measurements (first-block density, table size, per-step profile) are lab-run and are declared as heuristics with their scope.

heuristics.statement: The condition set of the published 36-step SHA-256 characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 (Tables 9 and 10: 57 uncontrolled conditions at steps >= 16, 15 first-block conditions on (E3,W5,W6,W7), the dense-part conditions at steps <= 15, and the message-expansion cancellations at indices 16,20,22,24,25,28,29,30), evaluated at rounds 0..31, is the complete set of conditions for a second-block collision at 32 steps: truncation from 36 to 32 steps removes no needed condition and adds none, and W31 is difference-free automatically.
heuristics.scope: The specific 2026/1120 36-step SHA-256 characteristic evaluated at rounds 0..31 from a chaining value satisfying its first-block conditions.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the published, executed 36-step attack to 32 steps (fewer rounds; identical condition set because the characteristic's support ends at index 30 and W31..W35 are difference-free automatically). Not an extrapolation to more rounds or to other characteristics.
heuristics.limitations: The published condition set is taken as complete for the published attack; the lab reproduced its counts and its conditional-probability profile but did not re-derive the characteristic with its own tool. The published paper reports the 36-step attack as executed and gives a colliding pair.

heuristics.statement: Distinct scanned candidates (B0, j), with B0 an accepted first block and j an entry of V, pass the step-16 test as independent events with probability at most 2^-12.4 each (2^-12.9 on average over V), and pass all 57 uncontrolled conditions (Table 9 rows 16..23 and Table 10 relations at i >= 16) as independent events with probability p_c each, so that among M*K candidates the number of survivors is binomially bounded and Pr[no collision] <= exp(-M*K*p_c).
heuristics.scope: Steps 16..23 of the 32-step characteristic with the dense part fixed by the SAT solution; conditions on A16..A21, E16..E21, W21, W23; candidates drawn from V across different accepted blocks.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard differential-attack accounting, validated at 36 steps by the published colliding pair obtained with the same 57-condition accounting, and here by measured per-step conditional profiles (42.94 measured vs 43 counted state conditions on the verified pair's (W14,W15); 12.9/15.75/6.0/7.0 vs 13/15/6/7 averaged over V) and by organizer-run local cancellation experiments.
heuristics.limitations: Joint dependence across steps 16..21, between state and W21/W23 conditions, and between candidates sharing a first block is not measured directly (the joint event has probability 2^-57.65); a parallel lab measurement with a different partition of the same conditions (proof Section 7.8) agrees on the total probability mass within about one bit. The sampled experiments test single 32-bit cancellations under uniform inputs, not the trail.

heuristics.statement: A uniformly random 64-byte first block B0 is accepted by the 15-condition first-block filter (E3[29]=1; signed differences of W5,W6,W7 as in Table 9; nine two-bit conditions of Table 10 on W5,W6,W7; dense part fixed) with probability q_true >= q = 2^-14.1; acceptance events of distinct trials are independent (fresh uniform blocks).
heuristics.scope: The block-1 trials of Section 6 Step 2 at 32 rounds from the standard IV, with the dense part fixed to the verified pair's solution.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured directly in this setting (final/cvrate.c: 2^28 uniform blocks compressed with 32 rounds from the standard IV, 16024 accepted, q = 2^-14.03, standard error 0.02 bits, per-condition-group breakdown in proof Section 7.2); the published 36-step measurement over 2^40 blocks gave 2^-15. The lower bound 2^-14.1 is used in the Chernoff bound of Section 7.7 and in N_b.
heuristics.limitations: Lab-run measurement, not an organizer execution; one dense solution; if the true density were 2^-15 the budget N_b would have to be 2^0.9 larger (total 2^52.77, still under the claim), and with the stated N_b the success bound would not hold.

heuristics.statement: The table V defined by the explicit chaining-value-independent conditions (V1)-(V5) of proof Section 6 has K = |V| <= K_max = 2^21.2 entries, and the per-accepted-block collision yield satisfies K * p_c >= y = 2^-37.2, where p_c is the probability that a scanned candidate passes all 57 uncontrolled conditions.
heuristics.scope: The dense solution of the verified pair (states A0..A13, E4..E13, words W8..W13 of ePrint 2026/1120 Table 2's second block); rows 14..23 of the characteristic.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured by enumeration and sampling (final/dcheck.c): exhaustive W14 over 2^32 gives 32 values satisfying (V1)-(V3); W15 acceptance for (V4)-(V5) is 2^-15.0 per admissible W14 (2^24 and 2^20 samples), so |V| = 2^20.98 and 2^21.12 in two runs; the per-step profile over 128 sampled entries of V gives p_c = 2^-57.65 and K p_c = 2^-36.67 (proof Sections 7.3, 7.4). The published attack reports 2^20 usable (W14,W15) with 57 conditions, i.e. the same yield 2^-37. The value y = 2^-37.2 is half a bit below the measurement.
heuristics.limitations: Lab-run measurements, not organizer executions; |V| is sampled for W15 (the exact count is produced by the enumeration of Step 1'); the step-17 average rests on 76 observed events (about 0.17 bits); each bit less of y adds one bit to the total (y = 2^-38 gives 2^53.2, above the claim).

heuristics.statement: An incremental evaluation of one compression step (and a few expansion adds) from precomputed chaining-value-independent state, carried out with ordinary 256-bit word operations, is charged at 1/2224 per operation under collision-frontier-v5, while every compression evaluated in full is charged one unit; the tail candidates are charged 32 operations each and the block-1 trials one unit each plus their check operations.
heuristics.scope: The cost ledger of Section 7.5; the tail scan of Section 6, Step 3.
heuristics.extrapolation: Direct reading of the cost model (one selected compression costs one unit; every other primitive word operation costs 1/C, with C derived from the operation count of one compression). No lane packing or parallel discount is used; total work is summed over all trials.
heuristics.limitations: If partial evaluations were priced as whole compressions the bound becomes 2^57.9 for the same fixed budget (Section 7.6); the claim's 2^53.0 depends on this pricing.
